item.title: ⚡️ Statement by the Russian Foreign Ministry on the terrorist attack in Jordan (October 24, 2026)
item.description: ⚡️ Statement by the Russian Foreign Ministry on the terrorist attack in Jordan (October 24, 2026) On October 23, an armed attack targeted people attending a memorial church service in the village of Hammoud, in Karak Governorate in western Jordan. According to preliminary reports, seven people were killed and another 40 sustained injuries of varying severity. ISIS has claimed responsibility for the attack. ❗️ We strongly condemn this cynical terrorist act , clearly aimed at undermining the interfaith peace and harmony established in Jordanian society. We consider attacks on religious sites and worshippers unacceptable . We reaffirm our unwavering solidarity with friendly Jordan in combating terrorism and extremism in all their manifestations. 🕯 We extend our sincere condolences to the leadership and people of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan and to the families and loved ones of those killed. We wish the injured a speedy recovery .

item.title: 👏 On October 21, the Museum of Moscow hosted the awards ceremony for the winners of
item.description: 👏 On October 21, the Museum of Moscow hosted the awards ceremony for the winners of the 12th Andrey Stenin International Press Photo Contest . An exhibition of this year’s winning and prize-winning entries also opened and will run until November 10. It includes photographs from the new Energy of Life category , introduced this year for photographers aged 34 and over. The Andrey Stenin International Press Photo Contest was established by the Rossiya Segodnya Media Group on December 22, 2014. It is named after Andrei Stenin , the media group’s special photojournalist and recipient of the Order of Courage, who was killed by Ukrainian militants near Donetsk in August 2014. The contest supports young photojournalists aged 18-33 in their pursuit of professional excellence, helping discover emerging talent and uphold high standards in documentary photography. Through their work, participants from around the world explore humanitarian challenges, national identity, social equality and environmental issues. *** 🏆 Grand Prix – Abdul Kader Al Bay ( #Lebanon ), for his series “Lebanon 2024-2025: Life Between Airstrikes” . item.title: ⚡️ #KievRegimeCrimes Ambassador-at-Large of the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
item.description: #KievRegimeCrimes ⚡️ Ambassador-at-Large of the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs Rodion Miroshnik : 💬 On October 22, another attempt was made to evacuate patients requiring specialist medical care from #Alyoshki to the district hospital in Skadovsk. Russian combat engineers had cleared the road after Ukrainian drones scattered mines along it overnight. However, Ukrainian artillery fire prevented the evacuation . ❗️ The ambulances were forced to turn around and return to Alyoshki . The video shows a nurse walking ahead, checking the road for mines, spikes and sharp fragments . Two ambulances follow her. Over the past year, mines and Ukrainian drone attacks have damaged or put out of service more than a dozen ambulances belonging to Alyoshki Hospital. ▪️ Earlier, two local residents with mine blast injuries died at Alyoshki Hospital . They needed specialist medical care but could not be evacuated due to a Ukrainian drone blockade of the roads .

🇺🇳
On October 24, 1945, the
Charter of the United Nations
entered into force. The date is celebrated as
United Nations Day
.
In February 1945, at the
Yalta Conference
, the leaders of the three Allied Powers – Stalin, Roosevelt and Churchill – agreed to convene the
San Francisco Conference,
where
50 countries signed the UN Charter
on 26 June 1945.
The establishment of the UN marked
the beginning of a new era in human history.
It was a natural consequence of World War II and reflected the international community’s determination to prevent such bloodshed from ever happening again and to
resolve conflicts through consensus and compromise
.
#UNCharterIsOurRules
: Russia consistently advocates strengthening the
central and coordinating role of the UN in world affairs
.
Strict adherence to the letter and spirit of the Charter is essential to building a more peaceful, prosperous, genuinely just and equitable world order.
🎙
From the address by Russian President
Vladimir Putin
at the plenary session of the
XVI BRICS Summit in the Outreach/BRICS Plus format
(24 October 2024)
:
The principles of the [UN Charter] <...> form the
foundation of interstate relations
and international law.
The United Nations is called upon to continue playing a
central role in maintaining peace and security
and promoting sustainable and steady growth.
The founding fathers of the United Nations envisioned it as a
centre for harmonising the actions of nations
.
👉
The role of the UN in the modern world was aptly described by
Vitaly Churkin
,
an outstanding Russian diplomat who served as Russia’s Permanent Representative to the UN from 2006 to 2017, in his remarks:
The UN has demonstrated its ability to adapt to the transformation of the international system.
At this time of turbulence in world affairs,
it is important to preserve the Organisation’s authority
, which rests on an enduring and truly democratic principle of functioning – the sovereign equality of all states, with no distinction between those who lead and those who follow.
Yet today, the Organisation is experiencing a
deep systemic crisis
, exacerbated by the
increasing politicisation of the Secretariat’s work
.
Russia’s position as regards the future of the UN and possible reforms was outlined by
Sergey Lavrov
in his
address
to the General Debate of
the 81st session
of the UN General Assembly
(New York, 26 September 2026)
:
Our principled position is that
reform of the Security Council must not entail allocating any additional seats to Western countries
, especially Germany and Japan, which have embarked on a path of militarisation and revanchism.
We exclusively support
increasing the representation of Asia, Africa and Latin America
. We support Brazil and India as candidates for permanent seats, while simultaneously – and I wish to emphasise this – ensuring that the interests of the African continent are met, in accordance with the Ezulwini Consensus and the Sirte Declaration.
❗️
We will continue to make every effort to fully restore the UN’s authority and standing.

Russian President Vladimir Putin's
address

the International Sports Forum “Russia: Country of Sports”
(October 23, 2026)
💬
I am delighted to greet the participants and guests of
the
International Sports Forum “Russia: Country of Sports”
.
This year, it is taking place in
Krasnoyarsk
, a city famous for its long-standing and excellent sports traditions. It is here on the banks of the Yenisei River that
several generations of legendary athletes and Olympic champions
grew up.
People who engage in sports activities and practice sports develop a better sense of responsibility and discipline
. They are better than others when it comes to focusing on achieving their objectives. These qualities enable them to succeed in their personal lives, as well as when serving their people and their country. This explains why
the Forum’s agenda
attaches great importance to children’s and teenage sports and efforts to promote physical activities among young people.
This track takes on special significance in the context of
the main theme for this year’s Forum
, which reads
“Sport: Uniting the World in Times of Change”
. Eras and periods of this kind shape the future and create conditions in which states and their people can continue developing.
At the same time, we know that
any changes or transformations would be impossible without a solid foundation
, and sport has a lot to offer in this regard. I am primarily referring to core human values such as
equality, justice, mutual respect and the unifying power of sport
. An overwhelming majority of nations share these values.
❗️
Russia has always been and will remain an integral and important part of this family
, while reaffirming its commitment to strictly following all the international obligations and justified requirements it assumes.
We are open to dialogue and cooperation and stand for preserving sports traditions
, the fundamental norms of international sports law, while also focusing on advancing and promoting development.
We believe that the future of sport consists of making it as accessible as possible
, proactively introducing innovative technology in training and competition, as well as in sports medicine, athlete training programmes and education.
🤝
We welcome the emergence of new sports disciplines
. What matters most is that they enable people to develop themselves in harmony while promoting a healthy lifestyle at a social level.

item.title: ⚡️ Statement by Press Secretary of the Russian President Dmitry Peskov on the humanitarian operation in Alyoshki, Kherson Region
item.description: ⚡️ Statement by Press Secretary of the Russian President Dmitry Peskov on the humanitarian operation in Alyoshki, Kherson Region * (October 23, 2026) Russia welcomes the efforts of US First Lady Melania Trump , who has made a substantial contribution to securing agreement on a humanitarian operation in Alyoshki , Kherson Region. To implement the agreements reached by the Presidents of Russia and the US, Russian Commissioner for Human Rights Yana Lantratova and her Ukrainian counterpart have carried out extensive work with Ms Trump’s direct involvement. Representatives of the defence ministries are coordinating the timing of a ceasefire (from 04:00 Moscow time on October 27, 2026) to enable the humanitarian mission in Alyoshki. ❗️ Those wishing to leave the city will be able to do so. The mission requires extensive and complex preparations involving a wide range of representatives. Melania Trump is playing a coordinating role . This issue was discussed during the recent telephone conversation between Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump. *Unofficial translation

🎙
Interview
by Director of the Russian MFA North Atlantic Department
Alexander Gusarov
with
International Affairs magazine
(October 22, 2026)
Key points
:
•
The North Atlantic Department is considered one of
the Ministry’s
most distinguished and well-established departments
, with a history dating back to the 1920s. Its formal founding date, regarded as its birthday,
is October 1, 1925.
•
We regard regular consultations between the Russian and US leaderships, as well as through other working channels, as
an important stabilising force in bilateral relations and the entire international security architecture.
•
Restoring a constructive approach to
#RussiaUSA
relations does not automatically resolve all the problems and disagreements
that have accumulated between our countries over the years. Clearly,
a great deal of painstaking work still lies ahead.
•
We have no doubt that US President Donald Trump is sincere in seeking mutually acceptable terms for a lasting and sustainable political settlement.
We appreciate the efforts made by
him personally
and
by his representatives
.
•
The current Republican majority in both houses of Congress
did not prevent the adoption of the rather
damaging “Lindsey Graham Russia and Iran Sanctions Act
”.
•
There is no reason to expect positive changes in Russia-UK relations following the formation of a new government in London.
We are convinced that London has no interest in normalising relations.
•
Russia-Canada relations remain at a near-zero level.
This stems from the Canadian leadership’s irrational obsession with anti-Russian illusions and Ottawa’s commitment to supporting the neo-Nazi Kiev regime.
•
Canada’s history contains
many controversial chapters
involving
Nazi criminals and collaborators who settled in the country after 1945.
•
We remain open to restoring normal relations with Ireland
, despite its drift towards the anti-Russian consensus in Brussels and London.

item.title: ⚡️ Russia's High Commissioner for Human Rights Yana Lantratova Today, on October 23,
item.description: ⚡️ Russia's High Commissioner for Human Rights Yana Lantratova : 💬 Today, on October 23, we are working in Belarus , where several important humanitarian missions are taking place. 🫂 The long-awaited reunification of families took place: seven people are returning to Russia, and another seven to Ukraine. Each person has their own story . Some had long been unable to return to their loved ones because of problems with documents. Others found themselves far from their families, without support or means of subsistence. Among those who returned home today are elderly people , for whom being alone is especially difficult. Ahead lie reunions with relatives, the long-awaited embraces they have missed so much, and the chance to be close to their loved ones again. ❗️ In total, today’s humanitarian initiative reunited 12 families. This work was made possible by agreements with the Ukrainian side and the assistance of the International Committee of the Red Cross . When people’s lives are at stake, it is especially important to maintain dialogue and find solutions despite the difficulties . My thanks go to Ukrainian Parliament Commissioner for Human Rights Dmitry Lubinets . We continue our work, because behind every appeal to return home are people waiting for their loved ones. And every reunion brings immense joy.
